stemMd: A town installed brighter streetlights and recorded fewer night-time collisions the next year. It concluded that the lights caused the reduction. Which information would most strengthen the conclusion?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The town also changed the colour of its logo.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Collisions had already fallen equally for five years before installation.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The new lights were more expensive than the old ones.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Comparable unmodified streets did not show a similar reduction during the same period.

explanationMd: A comparison group helps distinguish the lighting intervention from broader changes affecting all streets. If similar unmodified streets did not improve, the specific treatment becomes a more plausible cause. It still does not prove causation beyond all doubt.

distractorRationale.c: Cost does not establish collision effects.
distractorRationale.a: This has no relevant connection to night-time collisions.
distractorRationale.d: Preference does not resolve the causal comparison.
distractorRationale.b: That would suggest an existing trend rather than strengthen attribution.
